steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

=== README
# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes and shows the
questions on the big screen; the audience answers on their phones.

This release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes under `/moderate`.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` checks the variables, creates or migrates the SQLite databases under `storage/`,
and runs the app in the foreground on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:$PORT`). The app is served over
plain HTTP and accepts any host name. `GET /up` returns `200` when the app is ready.

Open `http://localhost:3000/moderate` and log in with the moderator credentials.

A quiz can be exported as JSON from its page ("Export") and imported as a new quiz from the quiz
list ("Import quiz"), on this or another Quizzy. See `docs/notes.md` for the format.
Everything under `/moderate` returns `401` without valid Basic credentials.

## Test it

```sh
bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
bin/rails test:system   # browser tests on the local Chromium (Cuprite, no chromedriver)
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman -q
```

The app and its tests run without network access: gems are installed locally and the
stylesheet, font and JavaScript are served from the repository.

## Docs

- `docs/notes.md`: design notes, routes, data rules, and decisions.
- `docs/mockups/`: the design's style guide and the two screens of this release.

# Quizzy: design notes

Working notes for the moderator release. Keep them current when the behaviour changes.

## Scope of this release

- Moderator area under `/moderate`, HTTP Basic (`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`).
- Quizzes, single-choice questions with text options, the "Active" switch, move up/down,
  delete, and the preview (a player's walk-through, nothing stored).
- Export and import of a quiz as JSON: "Export" on the quiz page, "Import quiz" on the quiz list.
- Not yet built: big-screen pages, player (phone) pages, live answers, scores over time.
  The stylesheet already has classes for them (`cover`, `stage-*`, `play-*`, `leader*`).

## Running

- `bin/serve` is the only entry point used in production. It needs `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and the two
  moderator variables (it stops with a message if one is missing), runs `bin/rails db:prepare`,
  and starts Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.
- Data: `storage/production.sqlite3` (app), plus `production_cache|queue|cable.sqlite3` from the
  default Solid* setup. Nothing else is written under `storage/`.
- HTTP only: `force_ssl` and `assume_ssl` are off; host authorization is not configured, so any
  host name is accepted. `/up` is Rails' health check (200 when booted).
- Assets: Propshaft serves `app/assets` itself in production (`config.assets.server = true`),
  because there is no proxy in front and no asset precompile step. `quizzy.css` and the font
  come from the design unchanged, apart from the font path. `moderator.css` holds app additions.
- No external calls. Turbo, Stimulus and importmap are vendored by their gems and served locally.

## Routes

| Page | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiz list | `GET /moderate` | "New quiz" is a GET button to the form |
| New quiz / save | `GET/POST /moderate/quizzes(/new)` | Saving opens the quiz page |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` | "Add question" (GET button), "Settings", "Preview" |
| Settings | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | Same form as new; "Delete quiz" with confirm |
| Export | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | Quiz as JSON in the only `<pre>`; "Export" link on the quiz page |
| Import form | `GET /moderate/imports/new` | "Import quiz" (GET button) on the quiz list; "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" button |
| Import | `POST /moderate/imports` | Always a new quiz; redirects to it (303). Errors: 422, nothing saved |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | State lives in the query string (see below) |
| New question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new` | Form, four empty rows, Active on |
| Create question",
  "output_tail": "con.ico` request).
- Layout: the header and `admin-main` follow the mockups; the preview uses the play layout
  (`layouts/preview.html.erb`) with the `play-*` classes.
- Phone check (390 px) and desktop check (1280 px): no horizontal overflow on any moderator
  page; Inter loads; background `#e9e6ff`.

## Gotchas

- `assert_difference` with an array uses one difference for every expression. Use a Hash.
- A model method that uses `order(...)` on an association that already has a default order
  appends to it. Use `reorder` (the move methods do).
- Capybara's `:button` finds `role="button"` only when `enable_aria_role` is on. The navigating
  "buttons" are therefore real `<button>`s inside GET forms.
- `rails new --skip-git` does not create `.gitignore`; one is in the repo.

## Tests

- `bin/rails test`: auth (401s, fail-closed when credentials are unset), quiz and question
  flows, option rules, move, activation, preview walk-through, model rules.
- `bin/rails test`, export and import: `test/integration/quiz_export_test.rb`,
  `test/integration/quiz_import_test.rb` (every rule, all-or-nothing, round trip),
  `test/models/quiz_import_test.rb`, `test/models/quiz_test.rb`.
- `bin/rails test:system`: Cuprite on `/usr/bin/chromium` with `no-sandbox`. Covers the Active
  auto-save, native confirm (accept and dismiss), Enter in an option field, Add option, the
  moderator flow end to end, the preview, and export then import through the browser
  (`test/system/quiz_transfer_test.rb`).
- `bin/rubocop` and `bin/brakeman -q` are clean. `bin/bundler-audit` needs GitHub and cannot run offline.

results.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy: design notes

Working notes for the moderator release. Keep them current when the behaviour changes.

## Scope of this release

- Moderator area under `/moderate`, HTTP Basic (`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`).
- Quizzes, single-choice questions with text options, the "Active" switch, move up/down,
  delete, and the preview (a player's walk-through, nothing stored).
- Export and import of a quiz as JSON: "Export" on the quiz page, "Import quiz" on the quiz list.
- Not yet built: big-screen pages, player (phone) pages, live answers, scores over time.
  The stylesheet already has classes for them (`cover`, `stage-*`, `play-*`, `leader*`).

## Running

- `bin/serve` is the only entry point used in production. It needs `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and the two
  moderator variables (it stops with a message if one is missing), runs `bin/rails db:prepare`,
  and starts Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.
- Data: `storage/production.sqlite3` (app), plus `production_cache|queue|cable.sqlite3` from the
  default Solid* setup. Nothing else is written under `storage/`.
- HTTP only: `force_ssl` and `assume_ssl` are off; host authorization is not configured, so any
  host name is accepted. `/up` is Rails' health check (200 when booted).
- Assets: Propshaft serves `app/assets` itself in production (`config.assets.server = true`),
  because there is no proxy in front and no asset precompile step. `quizzy.css` and the font
  come from the design unchanged, apart from the font path. `moderator.css` holds app additions.
- No external calls. Turbo, Stimulus and importmap are vendored by their gems and served locally.

## Routes

| Page | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiz list | `GET /moderate` | "New quiz" is a GET button to the form |
| New quiz / save | `GET/POST /moderate/quizzes(/new)` | Saving opens the quiz page |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` | "Add question" (GET button), "Settings", "Preview" |
| Settings | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | Same form as new; "Delete quiz" with confirm |
| Export | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | Quiz as JSON in the only `<pre>`; "Export" link on the quiz page |
| Import form | `GET /moderate/imports/new` | "Import quiz" (GET button) on the quiz list; "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" button |
| Import | `POST /moderate/imports` | Always a new quiz; redirects to it (303). Errors: 422, nothing saved |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | State lives in the query string (see below) |
| New question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new` | Form, four empty rows, Active on |
| Create question | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions` | Also handles "Add option" (no save) |
| Edit question | `GET /moderate/questions/:id/edit` | |
| Update / delete | `PATCH/DELETE /moderate/questions/:id` | Delete asks with `confirm()` |
| Move | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/move_up` and `/move_down` | Swaps with the neighbour in list order |
| Active switch | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/activation` | Form submits on change (Stimulus `auto-submit`) |

## Data

- `quizzes(title)`, `questions(quiz_id, text, position, active)`, `options(question_id, text, correct, position)`.
- Positions are unique per quiz and only swapped, never renumbered. A new question gets `max + 1`.
- Deleting a quiz or question deletes its options (dependent destroy).

## Option rules (`Question`)

Rows are `{text, correct}` as typed, including empty ones. On save:

1. Rows with blank text are dropped (their checkbox is ignored too).
2. Fewer than two filled rows: "Add at least two options".
3. No correct filled row: "Mark at least one option as correct".
4. An option over 200 characters: "Options can be at most 200 characters long".

Both 2 and 3 are reported together when both fail. Nothing is saved on failure, and the form is
re-rendered with 422 and exactly what was typed. The options are replaced inside the question's
save transaction, so the stored options never change on a failed save. "Active" alone saves
without touching options (`option_rows` is not assigned, so the rules do not run).

## Form details

- Option rows are named `question[options][i][text]` / `[correct]`. Labels: a visually hidden
  "Option N" for the text field (placeholder "Option text"), and a visible "Option N is correct"
  next to the checkbox. Both are real `<label>`s, so QA can find them by label text.
- "Add option" is a submit button with `formnovalidate`, `name=add_option`. The controller adds one
  empty row and re-renders with 200. Nothing is saved.
- Enter in an option field would submit through the first submit button in DOM order. A hidden
  `<button>` with no text comes first in the form, so Enter saves (tested in the system tests).
- The question form has `data-turbo="false"`: it re-renders with plain HTML responses.
- Edit shows the stored options plus empty rows, padded to four rows, like a new question.

## Quiz page

- Questions are an ordered list (`li",
  "output_tail": "als the number of active
  questions. Score = picks whose option is correct. Unknown or foreign option ids count as wrong.
- "Next question" and "See score" are GET forms that repeat `answers[]` plus the pick.
- Works without JavaScript. "Start over" is a GET form to the bare preview URL.

## Export and import

- Format: `{"title": ..., "questions": [{"text", "active", "options": [{"text", "correct"}]}]}`.
  Export writes exactly these keys, always with `active` and `correct`, pretty-printed. Nothing else:
  no ids, timestamps or positions. The order of the lists is the order of the quiz.
- Export page: `pre.code-block` is the only `<pre>` on the page (the layout has none). Inactive
  questions are exported too, with `"active": false`. Logic in `Quiz#export_data`.
- Import (`QuizImport`, `app/models/quiz_import.rb`): always creates a new quiz, even when a quiz
  with the same title exists. On success it redirects to the new quiz with "Quiz imported.".
- Lenient on purpose: `active` defaults to true, `correct` to false, and a `null` counts as missing.
  Keys outside the format are ignored. A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start is skipped.
- Strict on purpose: `title`, `text` and option `text` must be strings; `active` and `correct` must
  be `true` or `false`; `questions` must be a list (it may be empty); options must be a list of
  objects; the document must be an object.
- Question rules are the question form's, checked by the `Question` model: text required (max 500),
  option rows with blank text are dropped (their correct box too), at least two filled options, at
  least one correct, option text at most 200 characters. Positions are 1..n in list order.
- Format first: type and structure errors ("must be a string", "must be a list", ...) are all
  reported, and the rule checks are skipped while any exist, so a bad value does not also show
  misleading rule errors such as "Add at least two options".
- All or nothing: once the format is right, the whole document is checked in memory (the quiz and
  every question, so all broken questions are reported), then saved in one transaction. Any error: 422, "Nothing was
  imported.", the pasted text stays in the text area, and no quiz, question or option is written.
- "Question N" counts every entry in the `questions` list, inactive ones included.
- Messages: "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON", "Paste the quiz JSON to import", "Quiz JSON must be an
  object with a title and a list of questions", "Quiz JSON needs a list of questions", "Title must be
  a string", "Question N must be an object", "Question N: text must be a string", "Question N: active
  must be true or false", "Question N: options must be a list", "Question N: option M must be an
  object", "Question N: option M text must be a string", "Question N: option M correct must be true
  or false". Rule errors reuse the model messages with "Question N: " in front, e.g.
  "Question 2: Add at least two options".
- `QuizImport#valid?` rebuilds its records each time it runs, and `save` after a successful save
  returns true without importing again.

## Visual decisions

- Stylesheet: the design's `quizzy.css` is used as is. Additions live in `moderator.css` and use
  its tokens. The font is referenced as `url("Inter-latin.woff2")` so Propshaft digests it.
- Favicon: the logo mark as an inline SVG data URI in `layouts/_head.html.erb` (no `/favicon.ico` request).
- Layout: the header and `admin-main` follow the mockups; the preview uses the play layout
  (`layouts/preview.html.erb`) with the `play-*` classes.
- Phone check (390 px) and desktop check (1280 px): no horizontal overflow on any moderator
  page; Inter loads; background `#e9e6ff`.

## Gotchas

- `assert_difference` with an array uses one difference for every expression. Use a Hash.
- A model method that uses `order(...)` on an association that already has a default order
  appends to it. Use `reorder` (the move methods do).
- Capybara's `:button` finds `role="button"` only when `enable_aria_role` is on. The navigating
  "buttons" are therefore real `<button>`s inside GET forms.
- `rails new --skip-git` does not create `.gitignore`; one is in the repo.

## Tests

- `bin/rails test`: auth (401s, fail-closed when credentials are unset), quiz and question
  flows, option rules, move, activation, preview walk-through, model rules.
- `bin/rails test`, export and import: `test/integration/quiz_export_test.rb`,
  `test/integration/quiz_import_test.rb` (every rule, all-or-nothing, round trip),
  `test/models/quiz_import_test.rb`, `test/models/quiz_test.rb`.
- `bin/rails test:system`: Cuprite on `/usr/bin/chromium` with `no-sandbox`. Covers the Active
  auto-save, native confirm (accept and dismiss), Enter in an option field, Add option, the
  moderator flow end to end, the preview, and export then import through the browser
  (`test/system/quiz_transfer_test.rb`).
- `bin/rubocop` and `bin/brakeman -q` are clean. `bin/bundler-audit` needs GitHub and cannot run offline.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  # The option form always shows at least this many rows.
  MIN_FORM_OPTION_ROWS = 4
  MAX_OPTION_LENGTH = 200

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  normalizes :text, with: ->(text) { text.strip }

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  validates :text, presence: true, length: { maximum: 500 }
  validate :option_rules, if: :option_rows_assigned?

  # Replaces the stored options with the filled rows, in the same transaction as the question.
  after_save :replace_options, if: :option_rows_assigned?

  # Rows as the moderator typed them, including empty ones: [{ text:, correct: }, ...].
  # Only used to (re)render the form and to save; empty rows are skipped on save.
  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      row = row.to_h.with_indifferent_access
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  # Rows for the form: what was typed, or the stored options padded with empty rows.
  def form_option_rows
    return @option_rows if option_rows_assigned?

    rows = options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct? } }
    rows + Array.new([ MIN_FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def filled_option_rows
    Array(@option_rows).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  # Swaps the position with the neighbour above (moderator list order). Returns false at the top.
  def move_up
    reload
    swap_position_with(quiz.questions.where(position: ...position).reorder(position: :desc, id: :desc).first)
  end

  # Swaps the position with the neighbour below. Returns false at the bottom.
  def move_down
    reload
    swap_position_with(quiz.questions.where(position: (position + 1)..).reorder(position: :asc, id: :asc).first)
  end

  private

  def option_rows_assigned?
    !@option_rows.nil?
  end

  def assign_position
    self.position ||= (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def option_rules
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if filled_option_rows.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") unless filled_option_rows.any? { |row| row[:correct] }
    if filled_option_rows.any? { |row| row[:text].strip.length > MAX_OPTION_LENGTH }
      errors.add(:base, "Options can be at most #{MAX_OPTION_LENGTH} characters long")
    end
  end

  def replace_options
    options.destroy_all
    filled_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      options.create!(text: row[:text], correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    options.reset
  end

  def swap_position_with(other)
    return false unless other

    transaction do
      mine = position
      update_column(:position, other.position)
      other.update_column(:position, mine)
    end
    true
  end
end

# Creates a new quiz, with its questions and options, from JSON in the export format:
#
#   { "title": "...", "questions": [ { "text": "...", "active": true,
#       "options": [ { "text": "...", "correct": false } ] } ] }
#
# `active` defaults to true and `correct` to false. Questions and options keep their order.
# Every question follows the rules of the question form (Question model). The whole document is
# checked before anything is written: when a rule breaks, nothing is saved, not the quiz and not
# any of its questions.
class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Validations

  attr_reader :quiz

  validate :read_document

  def initialize(json_text)
    @json_text = json_text.to_s
    @quiz = nil
    @questions = []
    @imported = false
  end

  # Returns true when the quiz and all its questions are saved. Saving again does not import twice.
  def save
    return true if @imported
    return false unless valid?

    Quiz.transaction do
      quiz.save!
      @questions.each { |question, _label| question.save! }
    end
    @imported = true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    errors.add(:base, error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    false
  end

  private

  # Runs on every validation, so it starts from nothing: records are never built twice.
  def read_document
    @quiz = nil
    @questions = []

    document = parse_json
    return if errors.any?

    unless document.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON must be an object with a title and a list of questions")
      return
    end

    @quiz = Quiz.new(title: string_value(document["title"], "Title"))
    questions = document.fetch("questions", nil)
    unless questions.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON needs a list of questions")
      return
    end

    questions.each_with_index { |raw, index| build_question(raw, index + 1) }
    # Format errors come first: the rule checks would only repeat them as misleading rule errors.
    check_records unless errors.any?
  end

  def parse_json
    unless @json_text.valid_encoding?
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON")
      return
    end

    text = @json_text.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").strip
    if text.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Paste the quiz JSON to import")
      return
    end

    JSON.parse(text)
  rescue JSON::ParserError
    errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON")
    nil
  end

  def build_question(raw, number)
    label = "Question #{number}"
    unless raw.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be an object")
      return
    end

    question = Question.new(
      quiz: quiz,
      text: string_value(raw["text"], "#{label}: text"),
      active: boolean_value(raw["active"], true, "#{label}: active"),
      position: number
    )
    question.option_rows = option_rows(raw["options"], label)
    @questions << [ question, label ]
  end

  def option_rows(raw_options, label)
    return [] if raw_options.nil?

    unless raw_options.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}: options must be a list")
      return []
    end

    raw_options.each_with_index.map do |raw, index|
      option_label = "#{label}: option #{index + 1}"
      unless raw.is_a?(Hash)
        errors.add(:base, "#{option_label} must be an object")
        next { text: "", correct: false }
      end

      {
        text: string_value(raw["text"], "#{option_label} text"),
        correct: boolean_value(raw["correct"], false, "#{option_label} correct")
      }
    end
  end

  # Runs the model rules on the quiz and on each question. Question errors carry the question's number.
  def check_records
    copy_errors(quiz, nil)
    @questions.each { |question, label| copy_errors(question, label) }
  end

  def copy_errors(record, label)
    return if record.valid?

    record.errors.full_messages.each do |message|
      errors.add(:base, label ? "#{label}: #{message}" : message)
    end
  end

  # A missing or null value is an empty string, which the model then rejects where text is required.
  def string_value(value, label)
    return "" if value.nil?
    return value if value.is_a?(String)

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be a string")
    ""
  end

  # A missing or null value takes the default; anything other than true or false is an error.
  def boolean_value(value, default, label)
    return default if value.nil?
    return value if value == true || value == false

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be true or false")
    default
  end
end

# Walks a moderator through the quiz as a player would. Nothing is stored: the state is the
# list of options picked so far (`answers`, one option id per active question, in order) plus
# the option picked for the current question (`pick`). Both come from the URL.
class QuizPreview
  attr_reader :quiz, :questions, :answers

  def initialize(quiz, answers: [], pick: nil)
    @quiz = quiz
    @questions = quiz.active_questions
    @answers = Array.wrap(answers).map(&:to_s).first(@questions.size)
    @pick = pick.to_s.presence
  end

  def total
    questions.size
  end

  def empty?
    questions.empty?
  end

  def finished?
    !empty? && answers.size >= total
  end

  # 1-based number of the question on screen.
  def number
    answers.size + 1
  end

  def current_question
    questions[answers.size] unless finished? || empty?
  end

  def picked_option
    return if current_question.nil? || @pick.nil?

    current_question.options.find { |option| option.id.to_s == @pick }
  end

  def answered?
    picked_option.present?
  end

  def last_question?
    number == total
  end

  # Answers including the pick for the current question; used by "Next question" / "See score".
  def answers_with_pick
    answers + [ picked_option.id.to_s ]
  end

  def score
    answers.each_with_index.count { |answer, index| correct_answer?(questions[index], answer) }
  end

  def correct_answer?(question, answer)
    question.options.any? { |option| option.correct? && option.id.to_s == answer.to_s }
  end
end

module Moderate
  # Everything under /moderate needs the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.
  class BaseController < ApplicationController
    REALM = "Quizzy moderator".freeze

    before_action :authenticate_moderator!

    private

    def authenticate_moderator!
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic(REALM) do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    # Fails closed: if the configured credentials are missing, nobody gets in.
    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      username_matches = ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username)
      password_matches = ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password.to_s, expected_password)
      username_matches && password_matches
    end
  end
end

      @question.destroy!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(quiz), notice: "Question deleted.", status: :see_other
    end

    def move_up
      @question.move_up
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@question.quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_down
      @question.move_down
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@question.quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    # The "Active" checkbox on the quiz page saves on its own.
    def activation
      @question.update!(active: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params[:active]) == true)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@question.quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_question
      @question = Question.find(params[:id])
    end

    # Saves the question with its options, or re-renders the form with what was typed.
    # "Add option" only adds an empty row: nothing is saved.
    def save_form(question, template)
      rows = submitted_option_rows
      adding_option = params[:add_option].present?
      rows << { text: "", correct: false } if adding_option

      question.assign_attributes(text: question_params[:text], active: active_value(question))
      question.option_rows = rows

      if adding_option
        render template, status: :ok
      elsif question.save
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(question.quiz), notice: "Question saved.", status: :see_other
      else
        render template, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def question_params
      params.require(:question).permit(:text, :active, options: %i[text correct])
    end

    # Rows arrive as question[options][0][text], [0][correct], [1][text], ... in display order.
    def submitted_option_rows
      rows = question_params[:options]
      return [] if rows.blank?

      rows.to_h.sort_by { |index, _row| index.to_i }.map { |_index, row| row }
    end

    def active_value(question)
      return question.active? unless question_params.key?(:active)

      ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(question_params[:active]) == true
    end
  end

steps.message:
I now have the full picture. Here is the plan before I write code:

- **Data:** a game is a snapshot of the quiz's active questions and options, so editing a quiz never changes a running or past game. Tables: `games`, `game_questions`, `game_options`, `players`, `answers`.
- **Live updates:** each live region polls a fragment endpoint with an ETag (304 when unchanged). Server pokes over Turbo Streams (a custom `quizzy_refresh` action) trigger an immediate refresh. Pokes carry no data, so no answer information leaks through the stream.
- **Correct answers:** rendered only in the closed and finished states.

I'll start with the migration.

class CreateGames < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def change
    create_table :games do |t|
      t.references :quiz, null: false, foreign_key: true
      t.string :code, null: false
      # lobby | open | closed | finished
      t.string :phase, null: false, default: "lobby"
      # 1-based position of the current game question; nil in the lobby.
      t.integer :current_position
      # Bumped on every phase change. Player pages use it in their ETag.
      t.integer :revision, null: false, default: 0

      t.timestamps
    end
    add_index :games, :code, unique: true

    create_table :game_questions do |t|
      t.references :game, null: false, foreign_key: true
      t.integer :position, null: false
      t.text :text, null: false
      t.datetime :opened_at

    add_index :game_questions, [ :game_id, :position ], unique: true

    create_table :game_options do |t|
      t.references :game_question, null: false, foreign_key: true
      t.integer :position, null: false
      t.string :text, null: false
      t.boolean :correct, null: false, default: false

    add_index :game_options, [ :game_question_id, :position ]

    create_table :players do |t|
      t.references :game, null: false, foreign_key: true
      t.string :name, null: false

# One run of a quiz. The game keeps its own copy of the quiz's active questions and their options
# (see `create_from_quiz!`), so editing or deactivating questions never changes a game that is
# running or was played.
#
# Phases:
#   lobby    players join, nothing is open yet
#   open     the current question takes answers
#   closed   the current question is closed and its results are shown
#   finished the game is over: no more joins, no more answers
#
# Every phase change bumps `revision`, and tells the screens and phones to reload (see `announce`).
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[ lobby open closed finished ].freeze
  # Join codes avoid look-alike characters (no 0, O, 1, I, L), so they can be read out loud.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[ 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z ].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, length: { is: CODE_LENGTH }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :revision, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Copies the quiz's active questions, in quiz order, with their options. Inactive questions
  # are left out, so a game skips them.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz)
      quiz.active_questions.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(text: question.text, position: position)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.game_options.create!(text: option.text, correct: option.correct?, position: option_position)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def finished? = phase == "finished"

  def question_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return if current_position.nil?

    game_questions.find_by(position: current_position)
  end

  # Questions that were closed, in order: the ones a player's score is counted over.
  def played_question_count
    game_questions.where.not(closed_at: nil).count
  end

  # Moderator transitions. Each returns true when it changed the game, false when the phase did
  # not allow it (for example, a second click on "Next").
  def start!
    transition do
      next false unless lobby? && game_questions.exists?

      open_question_at!(1)
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    transition do
      next false unless open?

      close_current_question!
      update!(phase: "closed")
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    transition do
      next false unless closed? && current_position < question_count

      open_question_at!(current_position + 1)
    end
  end

  # Ends the game from any phase before "finished". A question that is still open is closed too.
  def end_quiz!
    transition do
      next false if finished?

      close_current_question! if open?
      update!(phase: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
    end
  end

  # A player joins. Returns the player, or nil when the game is over (the record then has errors).
  def join(name)
    return nil if finished?

    player = Player.new(game: self, name: name)
    return nil unless player.save

    announce(:screen)
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the current question. The last pick counts.
  # Returns :recorded, or the reason it was refused.
  def record_answer(player, option_id)
    return :not_joined unless player&.game_id == id

    question = current_question
    return :closed unless open? && question&.opened_at && question.closed_at.nil?

    option = question.game_options.find_by(id: option_id)
    return :unknown_option if option.nil?

    save_answer(player, question, option)
    announce(:screen)
    :recorded
  end

  # What the moderator's screen shows. A change in any of these reloads it.
  def screen_fingerprint
    [ revision, phase, players.count, answered_count ]
  end

  # What a player's page shows.
  def player_fingerprint(player)
    answer = player && current_question && player.answers.find_by(game_question: current_question)
    [ revision, phase, player&.id, answer&.game_option_id, answer&.updated_at&.to_f ]
  end

  def answered_count
    question = current_question
    question ? question.answers.count : 0
  end

  # The live pages subscribe to two streams. Pokes carry no data: the pages fetch their own
  # state, so no page ever gets another player's answer or the correct answers early.
  def announce(channel)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_action_to(self, channel, action: :quizzy_refresh, render: false)
  end

  private

  def assign_code
    self.code ||= loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      break candidate unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  # Runs the block under a row lock, bumps the revision when it returns truthy, and reloads the
  # screens after the commit.
  def transition
    changed = with_lock do
      changed = yield
      if changed
        self.revision += 1
        save!
      end
      changed
    end
    if changed
      announce(:screen)
      announce(:players)
    end
    changed
  end

  def open_question_at!(position)
    game_questions.find_by!(position: position).update!(opened_at: Time.current, closed_at: nil)
    update!(phase: "open", current_position: position)
  end

  def close_current_question!
    current_question&.update!(closed_at: Time.current)
  end

  def save_answer(player, question, option)
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
    answer.update!(game_option: option)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Two requests from the same player raced to create the answer. The second one updates it.
    retry
  end
end

# A live page keeps one region up to date by polling a fragment of itself. Each fragment carries an
# ETag over the state it shows, so a poll that finds nothing new gets a 304 and no HTML.
module LiveRegion
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def live_etag(parts)

class PlayController < ApplicationController
  include LiveRegion

  layout "play"

  ANSWER_REFUSALS = {
    not_joined: "Join the quiz first.",
    closed: "This question is closed.",
    unknown_option: "That question is no longer open."
  }.freeze

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :set_player
  before_action :set_live_etag

  def show
  end

  def live
    render_live_fragment(@live_etag)
  end

  def join
    return redirect_to(play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other) if @player || @game.finished?

    player = @game.join(params[:name].to_s)
    if player.persisted?
      cookies.permanent.encrypted[player_cookie_name] = { value: player.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      @join = player
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def answer
    result = @player ? @game.record_answer(@player, params[:option_id]) : :not_joined
    flash[:alert] = ANSWER_REFUSALS.fetch(result, "Your answer was not saved.") unless result == :recorded
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  # The browser that joined keeps its player's token, one cookie per game.
  def set_player
    token = cookies.encrypted[player_cookie_name]
    @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
  end

  def set_live_etag
    @live_etag = live_etag(@game.player_fingerprint(@player))
  end

  def player_cookie_name
    "quizzy_player_#{@game.code}"
  end
end

    end

        end

        if standalone
          output_tag.result.unshift(xml_tag, open_tag)
          output_tag.result << close_tag

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionCable::TestHelper

  setup do

    game.reload
  end

  test "a game copies the active questions in quiz order and skips inactive ones" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_equal [ "First?", "Third?" ], game.game_questions.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], game.game_questions.map(&:position)
    assert_equal [ "A1", "A2" ], game.game_questions.first.game_options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true ], game.game_questions.first.game_options.map(&:correct)
    assert_equal 2, game.question_count
    assert game.lobby?
  end

  test "editing the quiz afterwards does not change a game" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    @quiz.questions.first.update!(text: "Changed")
    @quiz.questions.first.options.first.update!(correct: true)

    assert_equal "First?", game.game_questions.first.text
    assert_equal false, game.game_questions.first.game_options.first.correct
  end

  test "each game of a quiz is separate, with its own players and answers" do
    first = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    second = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    refute_equal first.id, second.id
    refute_equal first.code, second.code
    assert_equal 2, @quiz.games.count
    assert_equal 2, first.question_count
    assert_not_equal first.game_questions.first.id, second.game_questions.first.id
  end

  test "join codes are five characters from the unambiguous alphabet" do
    20.times { Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz) }

    Game.all.each do |game|
      assert_match(/\A[2-9A-HJKMNP-Z]{5}\z/, game.code)
    end
    assert_equal Game.count, Game.distinct.count(:code)
  end

  test "start opens the first question, and only from the lobby" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert game.start!
    game.reload
    assert game.open?
    assert_equal 1, game.current_position
    assert_equal "First?", game.current_question.text
    assert game.current_question.opened_at
    refute game.start!, "a second start changes nothing"
  end

  test "a game without questions cannot start" do
    empty = create_quiz("Empty", questions: [])
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(empty)

    refute game.start!
    assert game.lobby?
  end

  test "finish closes the question, and only an open question can be finished" do
    game = started_game

    assert game.finish_question!
    game.reload
    assert game.closed?
    assert game.current_question.closed_at
    refute game.finish_question!
  end

  test "next moves to the next game question, skipping inactive quiz questions" do
    game = started_game
    game.finish_question!

    assert game.next_question!
    game.reload
    assert game.open?
    assert_equal 2, game.current_position
    assert_equal "Third?", game.current_question.text
  end

  test "next is refused while the question is still open or on the last question" do
    game = started_game
    refute game.next_question!, "no next question while one is open"

    game.finish_question!
    game.next_question!
    game.reload
    game.finish_question!
    refute game.reload.next_question!, "the last question has no next"
    assert game.closed?
  end

  test "end quiz finishes the game from any phase, closing an open question" do
    game = started_game

    assert game.end_quiz!
    game.reload
    assert game.finished?
    assert game.finished_at
    assert game.current_question.closed_at, "the open question is closed"
    refute game.end_quiz!
  end

  test "every phase change bumps the revision and tells the screen and the phones" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_broadcasts(game_stream(game, :screen), 1) do
      assert_broadcasts(game_stream(game, :players), 1) do
        game.start!
      end
    end
    assert_equal 1, game.reload.revision
  end

  test "a refused transition does not bump the revision or broadcast" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_no_broadcasts(game_stream(game, :players)) do
      refute game.finish_question!
    end
    assert_equal 0, game.reload.revision
  end

  test "a join appears on the screen only, not on the phones" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_broadcasts(game_stream(game, :screen), 1) do
      assert_no_broadcasts(game_stream(game, :players)) do
        game.join("Alice")
      end
    end
  end

  test "join adds a player, and a finished game does not let anyone join" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    player = game.join("  Alice  ")
    assert player.persisted?
    assert_equal "Alice", player.name
    assert player.token.present?

    game.end_quiz!
    assert_nil game.reload.join("Bob")
    assert_equal 1, game.players.count
  end

  test "a blank or over-long name is refused with a message" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    blank = game.join("   ")
    refute blank.persisted?
    assert_equal [ "Enter your name" ], blank.errors[:name]

    refute long.persisted?
    assert long.errors[:name].any?
    assert_equal 0, game.players.count
  end

    game = started_game
    alice = game.join("Alice")
    question = game.current_question
    wrong, right = question.game_options.to_a

    assert_equal :recorded, game.record_answer(alice, wrong.id)
    assert_equal :recorded, game.record_answer(alice, right.id)

    assert_equal 1, Answer.where(player: alice, game_question: question).count
    assert_equal right, Answer.find_by(player: alice, game_question: question).game_option
  end

  test "a pick is refused when the question is not open, or the option is not of this question" do
    game = started_game
    alice = game.join("Alice")
    other_question_option = game.game_questions.last.game_options.first

    assert_equal :unknown_option, game.record_answer(alice, other_question_option.id)
    assert_equal :unknown_option, game.record_answer(alice, "nope")

    game.finish_question!
    assert_equal :closed, game.reload.record_answer(alice, game.game_questions.first.game_options.first.id)
    assert_equal 0, Answer.count
  end

  test "a pick from someone who did not join this game is refused" do
    game = started_game
    other_game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    stranger = other_game.join("Stranger")
    option = game.current_question.game_options.first

    assert_equal :not_joined, game.record_answer(stranger, option.id)
    assert_equal :not_joined, game.record_answer(nil, option.id)
  end

  test "the screen and the phones fingerprints change when the game changes" do
    game = started_game
    alice = game.join("Alice")
    before_pick = game.player_fingerprint(alice)
    screen_before = game.screen_fingerprint

    game.record_answer(alice, game.current_question.game_options.first.id)
    assert_equal before_pick.first, game.reload.player_fingerprint(alice).first
    assert_not_equal before_pick, game.player_fingerprint(alice)
    assert_not_equal screen_before, game.screen_fingerprint
  end

  test "a player's score counts correct picks on closed questions only" do
    game = started_game
    alice = game.join("Alice")
    game.record_answer(alice, game.current_question.game_options.find_by(correct: true).id)
    game.finish_question!
    game.next_question!
    game.reload
    game.record_answer(alice, game.current_question.game_options.find_by(correct: false).id)

    assert_equal 1, alice.score, "the open question does not count yet"

    game.finish_question!
    assert_equal 1, alice.reload.score
    assert_equal 2, game.reload.played_question_count
  end

  private

  def game_stream(game, channel)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcasting_for([ game, channel ])
  end
end

require "test_helper"

# Each phone is its own integration session: its own cookies, so its own player.
class PlayTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
    @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
  end

  # A phone that joins the game under `name`; returns its session.
  def join_as(name)
    phone = open_session
    phone.post play_join_path(@game.code), params: { name: name }
    phone.assert_response :see_other
    phone
  end

  def option(question_position, text)
    @game.game_questions.find_by!(position: question_position).game_options.find_by!(text: text)
  end

  test "the join page asks for a name with a Join button, and needs no account" do
    get play_path(@game.code)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_select "label", text: "Your name"
    assert_select "input[name=name][type=text]"
    assert_select "button", text: "Join"
    assert_select "h1", text: "Frontend Fest 2026"
  end

  test "joining shows Hi, <name>! and the waiting state, and the browser remembers the player" do
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select "h1", text: "Hi, Alice!"
    assert_includes alice.response.body, "Waiting for the quiz to start"
    alice.assert_select "input[name=name]", count: 0
    assert_equal 1, @game.players.count

    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select "h1", text: "Hi, Alice!"
    assert_equal 1, @game.players.count, "opening the join link again does not add a player"
  end

  test "joining again from the same browser does not create a second player" do
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.post play_join_path(@game.code), params: { name: "Alice again" }
    alice.assert_redirected_to play_path(@game.code)
    assert_equal [ "Alice" ], @game.players.reload.map(&:name)
  end

  test "each browser is its own player" do
    join_as("Alice")
    bob = join_as("Bob")

    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], @game.players.reload.map(&:name)
    bob.get play_path(@game.code)
    bob.assert_select "h1", text: "Hi, Bob!"
  end

  test "a blank name is refused with the message, and nobody joins" do
    post play_join_path(@game.code), params: { name: "  " }
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select ".errors li", text: "Enter your name"
    assert_select "input[name=name]"
    assert_equal 0, @game.players.count
  end

  test "a finished game does not let anyone join, and its join link says the quiz is over" do
    @game.end_quiz!

    get play_path(@game.code)
    assert_select "h1", text: "The quiz is over"
    assert_select "input[name=name]", count: 0

    assert_no_difference "Player.count" do
      post play_join_path(@game.code), params: { name: "Late" }
    end
    assert_redirected_to play_path(@game.code)
  end

  test "during an open question the phone shows the options as buttons, and nothing about the answer" do
    @game.start!
    phone = join_as("Alice")
    phone.get play_path(@game.code)

    phone.assert_select "button[name=option_id]", count: 2
    phone.assert_select "button", text: /418/
    phone.assert_select "button", text: /429/
    phone.assert_select "form[action=?]", play_answers_path(@game.code)
    assert_no_match(/correct/i, phone.response.body)
    assert_no_match(/Right answer/, phone.response.body)
    assert_no_match(/Your answer/, phone.response.body)
    assert_no_match(/is-correct/, phone.response.body)
    assert_no_match(/data-correct/, phone.response.body)
  end

  test "tapping an option answers it, it is marked Your answer, and the last pick counts" do
    @game.start!
    alice = join_as("Alice")

    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "418").id }
    alice.follow_redirect!
    alice.assert_select "button.is-picked", text: /418/
    alice.assert_select "button.is-picked .play-option__mark", text: "Your answer"

    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    alice.follow_redirect!
    alice.assert_select "button.is-picked", text: /429/
    alice.assert_select "button.is-picked", text: /418/, count: 0
    assert_equal 1, @game.game_questions.first.answers.count
    assert_equal option(1, "429"), @game.game_questions.first.answers.first.game_option
  end

  test "a late joiner can answer the question that is open" do
    @game.start!
    late = join_as("Late")
    late.get play_path(@game.code)
    late.assert_select "button[name=option_id]", count: 2
  end

  test "a pick is refused when the question is closed, and the earlier pick stays" do
    @game.start!
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "418").id }
    @game.finish_question!

    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    alice.follow_redirect!
    alice.assert_select ".flash", text: "This question is closed."
    assert_equal option(1, "418"), @game.game_questions.first.answers.first.game_option
  end

  test "a pick from a browser that has not joined is refused" do
    post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    assert_redirected_to play_path(@game.code)
    follow_redirect!
    assert_select ".flash", text: "Join the quiz first."
    assert_equal 0, Answer.count
  end

  test "after Finish the phone shows Correct!, Wrong! or No answer, and the right option" do
    @game.start!
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    bob = join_as("Bob")
    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    bob.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "418").id }
    @game.finish_question!

    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select ".play-status--right", text: "Correct!"
    alice.assert_select "button", count: 0
    alice.assert_select ".play-option.is-correct", text: /429/
    alice.assert_select ".play-option.is-picked .play-option__mark", text: "Your answer"

    bob.get play_path(@game.code)
    bob.assert_select ".play-status--wrong", text: "Wrong!"

    carol = join_as("Carol")
    carol.get play_path(@game.code)
    carol.assert_select ".play-status--neutral", text: "No answer"
  end

  test "the next question replaces the result, and the end shows the score" do
    @game.start!
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    @game.finish_question!
    @game.next_question!

    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select ".play-question__num", text: "Question 2 of 2"
    alice.assert_select "button[name=option_id]", count: 2

    @game.finish_question!
    @game.end_quiz!
    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select "h1", text: "The quiz is over"
    alice.assert_select ".result-card__score", text: "Your score: 1 of 2"
  end

  test "the phone's live fragment answers 304 until its own state changes" do
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_response :ok
    etag = alice.response.headers["ETag"]

    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code), headers: { "If-None-Match" => etag }
    alice.assert_response :not_modified

    @game.start!
    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code), headers: { "If-None-Match" => etag }
    alice.assert_response :ok, "a new question changes every phone"
    assert_no_match(/<html/, alice.response.body)
    alice.assert_select "#live[data-live-etag-value=?]", alice.response.headers["ETag"]
  end

  test "an unknown join link is not found" do
    get "/play/NOPE1"
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "the join code is not case sensitive" do
    get "/play/#{@game.code.downcase}"
    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "the score is not shown to a visitor who never joined" do
    @game.end_quiz!
    get play_path(@game.code)
    assert_select ".result-card__score", count: 0
  end
end
EOF

# session (so its own cookies and its own player). Every change must show up without a reload.
class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  test "the big screen and the phones follow a game live" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text
    assert_match %r{/play/[2-9A-HJKMNP-Z]{5}\z}, join_url
    page.execute_script("window.screenMarker = 'same page'")

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
      assert_text "Waiting for the quiz to start"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 2"
    assert_no_text "Question 1 of"

    click_on "Start"
    assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    assert_no_text "Correct"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
      click_button "418"
      assert_text "Your answer"
      click_button "429"
      assert_button "429"
      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "429"
      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "Your answer"
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    click_on "Finish"
    assert_text "Correct"
    assert_css "li.stage-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      assert_css ".play-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "No answer"
    end

    click_on "Next"
    assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
      click_button "WebSocket"
      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "WebSocket"

    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    click_on "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_text "Your score: 2 of 2"
    end

    assert_equal "same page", page.evaluate_script("window.screenMarker"), "the big screen never reloaded"
  end

  test "a late change still reaches the big screen when the live pokes are lost" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

        click_on "Join"
        assert_text "Hi, Carol!"
      end
      using_wait_time(8) { assert_text "Players: 1" }
    end
  end
end

class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [

      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]

  test "the big screen and the phones follow a game live" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)

      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"

    assert_live_text "Players: 2"
    assert_no_text "Question 1 of"

    click_on "Start"
    assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_live_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    assert_no_text "Correct"

      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "418"
      click_button "429"
      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "429"
      assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "Your answer"

    assert_css "li.stage-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

      assert_css ".play-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_live_text "No answer"
    end

    assert_live_text "Question 2 of 2"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 2 of 2"

    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    without_pokes do

    original = Turbo::StreamsChannel.method(:broadcast_action_to)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to) { |*, **| nil }
    yield
  ensure
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to, original)
  end
end

mkdir -p /tmp/e2e && cat > /tmp/e2e/prod_flow.rb <<'EOF'
require "capybara"
require "capybara/cuprite"
require "base64"

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"
Capybara.register_driver(:cuprite_prod) do |app|
  Capybara::Cuprite::Driver.new(app, browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true,
    window_size: [ 1280, 900 ], browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil }, js_errors: true, timeout: 20, process_timeout: 60)
end
Capybara.default_driver = :cuprite_prod
Capybara.run_server = false
Capybara.app_host = BASE
Capybara.default_max_wait_time = 4

def timed(label)
  started = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  yield
  puts format("  ok %-42s %.2fs", label, Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - started)
end

mod = Capybara.current_session
mod.driver.browser.headers.set("Authorization" => "Basic " + Base64.strict_encode64("moderator:s3cret-pass"))
mod.visit "/moderate"
mod.visit "/moderate/quizzes/1"
mod.click_on "Start a game"
mod.assert_text "Players: 0"
join_url = mod.find(".lobby__url").text
puts "join link: #{join_url}"
puts "qr svg present: #{mod.has_css?('figure.qr svg')}"
mod.execute_script("window.marker = 'same page'")

alice = Capybara::Session.new(:cuprite_prod, nil)
alice.visit join_url
alice.fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
timed("alice joins -> screen Players: 1") do
  alice.click_on "Join"
  alice.assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
  mod.assert_text "Players: 1"
end
bob = Capybara::Session.new(:cuprite_prod, nil)
bob.visit join_url
bob.fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
bob.click_on "Join"
bob.assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
timed("bob joined -> Players: 2") { mod.assert_text "Players: 2" }

timed("start -> question on screen and phones") do
  mod.click_on "Start"
  mod.assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
  alice.assert_text "Too Many Requests"
  bob.assert_text "Too Many Requests"
end
timed("alice taps 418 (wrong), then 429 (right)") do
  alice.click_button "418"
  alice.assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "418"
  alice.click_button "429"
  alice.assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "429"
end
timed("screen Answers: 1 / 2") { mod.assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2" }
timed("finish -> screen counts + Correct") do
  mod.click_on "Finish"
  mod.assert_text "Correct"
end
timed("phones show result") do
  alice.assert_text "Correct!"
  bob.assert_text "No answer"
end
puts "  screen marker still: #{mod.evaluate_script('window.marker')}"
timed("next -> question 2 everywhere") do
  mod.click_on "Next"
  mod.assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
  alice.assert_text "Which protocol is two-way?"
end
alice.click_button "WebSocket"
alice.assert_css "button.is-picked", text: "WebSocket"
mod.assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"
mod.click_on "Finish"
mod.click_on "End quiz"
timed("end -> The quiz is over on screen and phones") do
  mod.assert_text "The quiz is over"
  alice.assert_text "The quiz is over"
  alice.assert_text "Your score: 2 of 2"
end
puts "  done"
EOF
cd /app && timeout 300 bundle exec ruby /tmp/e2e/prod_flow.rb 2>&1 | tail -40

require "application_system_test_case"

# A whole game in the browser: the moderator's big screen and two phones, each in its own browser
# session (so its own cookies and its own player). Changes must show up without a reload.
class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  test "the big screen and the phones follow a game live" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_live_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text
    assert_match %r{/play/[2-9A-HJKMNP-Z]{5}\z}, join_url
    page.execute_script("window.screenMarker = 'same page'")

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_live_text "Hi, Alice!"
      assert_text "Waiting for the quiz to start"
    end
    assert_live_text "Players: 1"

    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_live_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    assert_live_text "Players: 2"
    assert_no_text "Question 1 of"

    click_on "Start"
    assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_live_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    assert_no_text "Correct"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
      click_button "418"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "418"
      click_button "429"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "429"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "Your answer"

  test "a change still reaches the big screen and the phones when the live pokes are lost" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

    # Lose every poke: only the regular checks of the pages can bring the changes in.
    without_pokes do
      Capybara.using_session(:carol) do
        visit join_url
        fill_in "Your name", with: "Carol"
        click_on "Join"
        assert_text "Hi, Carol!"
      end
      using_wait_time(8) { assert_text "Players: 1" }
    end
  end

  test "a name typed on the phone is kept when the page refreshes" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

    Capybara.using_session(:dana) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Dana"
      # Marks this input, so that it can be told apart from the one the refresh draws.
      page.execute_script("document.getElementById('player_name').dataset.before = 'yes'")
    end

    # Starting the game changes the join page, so the phone redraws its region.
    click_on "Start"
    Capybara.using_session(:dana) do
      assert_no_selector "#player_name[data-before]"
      assert_field "Your name", with: "Dana"
      assert_equal "player_name", page.evaluate_script("document.activeElement.id")
    end
  end

  private

  # Pokes arrive within about a second. The pages also check on their own every 2-3 seconds, so
  # a longer wait would pass even without the live push.
  def assert_live_text(text)
    using_wait_time(1.5) { assert_text(text) }
  end

  # Makes the server send no pokes for the duration of the block.
  def without_pokes
    original = Turbo::StreamsChannel.method(:broadcast_action_to)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to) { |*, **| nil }
    yield
  ensure
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to, original)
  end
end

live = <<'LIVE'

## Live game

### Game = a snapshot

- `Game.create_from_quiz!` copies the quiz's **active** questions, in quiz order, with their options
  and correct flags. Inactive questions are left out, so a game skips them. The game never reads the
  quiz again: editing or deleting questions changes neither a running game nor a past one.
- Each start of "Start a game" is a new game with its own code, players and answers. Rehearsals and
  the real talk do not share anything.
- Join codes: 5 characters from `Game::CODE_ALPHABET` (no 0, O, 1, I, L), unique.

### Phases

| Phase | Meaning | Moderator's button | Phones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lobby` | Players join, nothing is open | "Start" (or "End quiz" when no question is active) | "Hi, <name>!" and waiting |
| `open` | The current question takes answers | "Finish" | Options as buttons, "Your answer" on the pick |
| `closed` | The question is closed, results shown | "Next", or "End quiz" on the last question | "Correct!", "Wrong!" or "No answer", the right option marked |
| `finished` | Over: no joins, no answers | (none, "Back to quiz") | "The quiz is over", the player's score |

- "End quiz" works from any phase. An open question is closed by it.
- Every step is a transition under `with_lock`. A step the phase does not allow returns false and
  changes nothing (no revision bump, no broadcast). The screen then shows a flash with the reason.
- `revision` goes up on every phase change. It is part of the ETags, so phones and screens notice.

### Counters and what they count

- Lobby: "Players: N" counts every player who joined this game.
- "Answers: x / y" (open and closed): `x` = players who answered the current question, `y` = all
  players in the game, including those who joined after the question opened.
- Scores: a player's score counts correct picks on closed questions. The end page shows
  "Your score: x of y" where `y` is the number of closed questions.

### The rule: no correct answer before the question is closed

- The phone's open-question markup has no `correct` flag, no `is-correct` class, no hint text. The
  options are buttons whose `value` is the option id. Tests check the HTML for "correct" (case
  insensitive) and for `is-correct`, `data-correct`, "Right answer" during the open phase.
- The big screen's open markup has no counts and no marks. Counts and the "Correct" marks come
  only in `closed`.
- Pokes (below) carry no data. The fingerprints (ETags) are numbers and ids, no answers. So no
  stream and no ETag ever reveals a correct answer early.
- A phone only ever gets its own player's state (the token is in its cookie).

### Who is the player

- Joining creates a `Player` with a random token (`SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)`).
- The token goes into a permanent, encrypted, httponly cookie named `quizzy_player_<CODE>`, one per
  game. Opening the join link again from that browser finds the player and continues. Another
  browser is another player, even with the same name.
- A finished game refuses joins. Its join link shows "The quiz is over" to everyone.

### Live updates

Two mechanisms, both without page reloads. They cover each other's gaps, which matters on crowded
Wi-Fi (missed messages, sleeping phones, dropped sockets):

1. **Pokes (push).** After a change the server broadcasts a Turbo stream with the custom action
   `quizzy_refresh` (`Game#announce`). Two streams per game: `[game, :screen]` for the big screen,
   `[game, :players]` for phones. Phase changes poke both. Joins and answers poke the screen only,
   so 200 phones answering do not make 200 phones reload. `app/javascript/application.js` registers
   the action; it dispatches a `quizzy:refresh` window event with no data.
2. **Polls (pull).** Every live region (`live` Stimulus controller, `app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
   asks its `live` fragment every 2 s (screen) or 3 s (phone). The fragment carries an ETag over the
   state it shows (`LiveRegion`, `Game#screen_fingerprint`, `Game#player_fingerprint`). Nothing new
   means `304` and no DOM work. Polls also run on `visibilitychange` (phone back in front) and `online`.

Client details that matter:

- A poke refresh waits a random 0-400 ms, so the room does not ask all at once. A refresh that is
  already in flight is followed by one more, never more than that.
- Responses are numbered; an older response never overwrites a newer one.
- The region is replaced as a whole (`innerHTML`). Text typed in the region is kept, and focus is
  put back (the name field of the join form must survive a refresh).
- Forms marked `data-live-form` are sent with `fetch`. The server answers with a redirect, and the
  page after the redirect provides the new region. Without JavaScript the same forms just work.
- Answers: the tapped option is marked at once. Only the latest tap is sent while one is in flight:
  "the last pick counts" also holds when requests arrive out of order.
- Steps and join buttons are disabled while their request is in flight, so a double click cannot
  start two steps. Answer buttons stay tappable.
- A failed send (network) triggers a refresh, which shows what the server really has.

Latency in the production check: join to big screen, start to phones, answer to screen: 0.1-0.5 s.
The lost-poke test shows that polls alone still bring every change in within about 3 seconds.

### Screens

- Big screen: `layouts/screen`, `cover` background (blue, night when over), the `screen-controls` bar
  at the bottom. Lobby: quiz title, join link as plain text (`http://host/play/CODE`, the same
  host the moderator used), QR code (`join_qr_svg`, one SVG path with a 4-module quiet zone),
  "Players: N".
- Phone: `layouts/play`, one column, big buttons. The top bar shows "Hi, <name>!" once joined.
- Both use the stylesheet's classes (`stage-*`, `lobby*`, `play-*`, `result-card`, `mark`).

### Gotchas

- A `fetch` from the big screen carries the moderator's Basic credentials once the browser has them.
  The system tests set them as headers, like the rest of the suite.
- Rails' ETag helper hashes the body, and the form tokens change on every render. So the ETag is
  built from the state (`LiveRegion#live_etag`), not from the HTML. Otherwise nothing is ever 304.
- `rqrcode`'s `as_svg(standalone: false)` returns the shapes without an `<svg>` wrapper, and its
  `standalone: true` output has an XML declaration that does not belong in HTML. The helper wraps it.
- `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcasting_for` adds a `turbo:streams:` prefix. The stream a page subscribes
  to, and the name tests must assert, is `Turbo::StreamsChannel.send(:stream_name_from, [game, :screen])`.
- Minitest 6 (in this bundle) has no `minitest/mock`. The system test swaps the broadcast method with
  `define_singleton_method` and restores it in `ensure`.
- In an integration test, `assert_select` reads the test's own last response. To check another phone,
  call `assert_select` on that session (`open_session`).

### Tests

- `test/models/game_test.rb`: snapshot, inactive questions, phases, refused steps, joins, answers,
  revision and broadcasts, score.
- `test/models/answer_test.rb`: an answer belongs to its option's question and to the player's game.
- `test/integration/games_test.rb`: credentials, "Start a game", the lobby, the counters, Finish and
  the correct marks, the last question, the live fragment with ETags, the quiz page's game list,

- `test/integration/play_test.rb`: joining, the cookie (rejoin, one player per browser), name errors,

  scores, the phone fragment with ETags.
- `test/system/live_game_test.rb`: a moderator and two phones, each in its own browser session.
  Every live change must show up within 1.5 s (push, not the 2-3 s poll), and the big screen's page
  must not reload. Also: the lost-poke run, and a typed name that survives a redraw.

cd /app && cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under `/moderate` and runs
games of them: the questions go up on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones,
with no account. Everything follows the game live.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` checks the variables, creates or migrates the SQLite databases under `storage/`,
and runs the app in the foreground on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:$PORT`). The app is served over
plain HTTP and accepts any host name. `GET /up` returns `200` when the app is ready.

Open `http://localhost:3000/moderate` and log in with the moderator credentials.

- Quizzes: create them, add questions (options, the correct ones, "Active"), preview them.
  A quiz can be exported as JSON from its page ("Export") and imported as a new quiz from the
  quiz list ("Import quiz"), on this or another Quizzy. See `docs/notes.md` for the format.
- Games: "Start a game" on a quiz page opens a game on the big screen. The lobby shows the join
  link and its QR code. Players open the link on their phones, enter a name, and answer. The
  moderator goes on with "Start", "Finish", "Next" and "End quiz".

Everything under `/moderate` returns `401` without valid Basic credentials. The phone pages under
`/play/<code>` are public: the code is the game's join link.

## Test it

```sh
bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
bin/rails test:system   # browser tests on the local Chromium (Cuprite, no chromedriver)
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman -q
```

The app and its tests run without network access: gems are installed locally and the
stylesheet, font and JavaScript are served from the repository.

## Docs

- `docs/notes.md`: design notes, routes, data rules, the live game, and decisions.
- `docs/mockups/`: the design's style guide and the screens of the moderator side.
EOF
